source_text:
Στίχ. β΄. Αὗται αἱ ἑορταὶ Κυρίου. Πᾶσα ἱλαρὰ ἡμέρα, ἐν ᾗ προτέτακται (19), ὡς ἐν ἁγίᾳ τάδε τινὰ ποιεῖν παρὰ τὰς λοιπὰς ἐξαίρετα, ἑορτὴ καλεῖται. Οὐ πᾶσα δέ ἐστι πανήγυρις· ἀλλὰ κατὰ τοὔνομα, ὅτε ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ συναθροίζονται πανταχόθεν. Ὥστε ἡ μὲν πανήγυρίς ἐστι καὶ ἑορτή· οὐκέτι δὲ ἑορτὴ, καὶ πανήγυρις· οἷον· Σάββατα καὶ Νουμηνίαι, ἑορταί εἰσιν· Ἄζυμα δὲ, καὶ ἡμέραι τῶν Ἑβδομάδων, καὶ Σκηνοπηγίαι οὐ μόνον ἑορταὶ, ἀλλὰ καὶ πανηγύρεις.
Στίχ. μ΄. Καὶ κάλλυντρα φοινίκων. Πάρεστι διὰ τούτων νοεῖν (20), καὶ πάλιν ἡμῖν ἐν Χριστῷ τὰς ἐν παραδείσῳ τρυφὰς ἀπονέμει Θεός. Φυτῶν δὲ τῶν ἀειθαλῶν οἱ κλάδοι, τὸ διηνεκὲς τῆς χάριτος καὶ τὸ ἀμάραντον τῆς ἐλπίδος ἐφʼ ἑαυτοῖς σημαίνουσι.
thought_title: Feasts, solemn assemblies, and evergreen branches
orientation: Origen is commenting on Leviticus 23, distinguishing which holy days are mere feasts and which are also solemn assemblies, then explaining the palm branches of the Feast of Tabernacles as signs of grace and hope in Christ.
pass_a_gloss: Verse 2. These [are] the feasts of the Lord. Every cheerful day, in which it has been prescribed, as in a holy [day], to do certain special things beyond the remaining [days], is called a feast. But not every [feast] is a solemn assembly; but according to the name, when they are gathered together to the same [place] from everywhere. So the solemn assembly is also a feast; but no longer [is every] feast also a solemn assembly; for example: Sabbaths and New Moons are feasts; but Unleavened Bread, and the days of the Weeks, and Tabernacles [are] not only feasts, but also solemn assemblies. Verse 40. And adornments of palms. It is possible through these to understand, and again to us in Christ God apportions the delights in paradise. And of the evergreen plants the branches signify on themselves the perpetual [quality] of grace and the unfading [quality] of hope.

choices.why: Keeps the literal adjective 'cheerful' for a day of prescribed holy actions, matching the source's positive tone.
Renders the perfect passive of προστάσσω as a standing prescription, preserving the force of an established command.
The adjective means 'chosen out, exceptional'; 'special things' keeps the sense of actions set apart from ordinary days.
Literal rendering of the idiom, preserving Origen's etymological point about πανήγυρις meaning a gathering of all.
κάλλυντρον means an ornament or adornment; 'adornments of palms' keeps the literal sense of the lemma.
ἀπονέμω means to assign or distribute as one's due; 'apportions' preserves the sense of God granting delights to us in Christ.

pass_b_english: Verse 2: “These are the feasts of the Lord” (Leviticus 23:2). Every cheerful day on which it has been prescribed to do certain special things as on a holy day, beyond what is done on the remaining days, is called a feast. But not every feast is a solemn assembly; rather, according to the name, it is when people are gathered together from everywhere to the same place. So a solemn assembly is also a feast, but a feast is not necessarily also a solemn assembly. For example, Sabbaths and New Moons are feasts, but Unleavened Bread, the days of the Weeks, and Tabernacles are not only feasts but also solemn assemblies.

Verse 40: “And adornments of palms” (Leviticus 23:40). Through these things it is possible to understand that God apportions to us again in Christ the delights of paradise. The branches of evergreen trees signify in themselves the perpetual nature of grace and the unfading quality of hope.

problems.why: Singular/plural drift in key term vs. usage; minor.
problems.fix: Use consistent number in key terms.

problems.why: Leviticus 23:40 LXX refers to branches of palm trees; 'adornments' is an odd rendering that obscures the botanical imagery Origen then interprets.
problems.fix: Use 'branches of palm trees' to match the evergreen branches discussion.

fixed: Glossary number drift: The English uses 'solemn assembly' consistently in the singular for the generic term and 'solemn assemblies' in the plural for specific instances, which matches the source's πανήγυρις/πανηγύρεις usage; no edit needed.
Mistranslation: Leviticus 23:40 LXX κάλλυντρα φοινίκων refers to branches of palm trees, and 'adornments' obscures the botanical imagery Origen interprets; changed to 'branches of palm trees'.
